title: Why Can't You Say "M" With Your Mouth OPEN? 👄
description:
Open your mouth wide and try to say "mmm". Can't? Nobody can. M is a hum that comes out of your NOSE: your lips shut, the soft palate at the back of your mouth hangs open, and the sound goes up and out through your nose (hum and touch the side of your nose: it buzzes). Open your lips and the hum takes the easy way out, through your mouth, and turns into "aaah". That's why you can't answer your dentist.
Did you get an M?

Bonus: ventriloquists can't make a real M without moving their lips either. They swap in an N and let your brain hear the M. Try "mama" with your lips still: you get "nana".
